task_snapshot.title: Recommend current files and symbols from task and co-change evidence
task_snapshot.description:
Daniel approved implementation of a standalone Orbit plugin learning from actual verified changes, with file/symbol modes; context_files must NOT be a training dependency or automatically mutated. Work only in orbit-graph; no Orbit control-plane crate dependencies or internal database reads. Preserve current graph/CLI behavior. No releases, tags, publication, or agent-review automation. Keep modules readable and cohesive. Run CONTRIBUTING.md checks, strict Clippy/fmt/tests/docs/build and real CLI tests; leave changes for managed delivery.

Stage 2 of 3, depends on the history index task. Read docs/design/change-recommendations.md and its public types after stage 1 lands. Implement library/CLI recommend accepting exactly one query or task ID, level=file|symbol, top-K limit, and explicit target revision (default current checkout). Task query uses title/description/acceptance criteria only; exclude target task's own delivery/summary and future evidence. Rank similar historical tasks and their verified changed locations, expand directional co-change associations, then bounded current structural neighbors (callers/callees/implementations/test links where evidence exists). Preserve a pluggable input for Orbit's existing hybrid search ranked hits (provided through stage 3 adapter), with deterministic local lexical retrieval for standalone/backtesting use; do not need a new embedding service. Normalize file aggregation so many symbols in one file do not unfairly multiply votes.

Explainable scoring combines task similarity, actual change evidence, co-change support/confidence/lift and bounded current structure, with recency decay and discounts for broad bulk changes, generated files/lockfiles, ubiquitous locations and ambiguous task association. Use each delivery once, not task-count-expanded pseudo-evidence. Cold start/empty history remains meaningful with explicit limited evidence. Return rank, score (not probability), selector, supporting task/delivery IDs, counts/directional association and contribution reasons, source freshness/index revision, resolved target revision, and explicit symbol-mode file fallbacks. Resolve historical identities through renames against CURRENT/requested revision; never suggest deleted or unresolved symbols as live destinations; stale/unavailable results must be explicit. Branch-specific databases and non-default target revisions must not silently use HEAD structure.

Use deterministic ranking tests and real CLI fixture tasks/history showing relevant function and tests outrank ubiquitous metadata, association asymmetry, scope size dilution, recency, file and symbol modes, deleted/renamed symbols, duplicate/ambiguous deliveries, temporal cutoff/self-leakage exclusion, stable ties and top-K validation. Do not make handpicked output-string tests the primary proof. Stage 3 implements protocol adapter and chronological evaluation; expose reusable scoring/baseline/cutoff seams without speculative frameworks.
acceptance_criteria: Query and task-ID recommendations work in both file and symbol modes with top-K, revision resolution, explanations and explicit fallback/freshness metadata.
Deterministic behavioral tests establish directional association support/confidence/lift, broad-change discounts, recency, deduplication and useful task relevance.
Target task/future delivery evidence is excluded; removed/unresolved symbols are never returned as live destinations, including rename and non-HEAD revision cases.
Existing graph commands continue passing; full CONTRIBUTING validation and real executable recommendation fixtures pass; documented public interfaces support integration/backtesting.

task_snapshot.title: Integrate Orbit recommendation plugin and chronological backtesting
task_snapshot.description:
Daniel approved implementation of a standalone Orbit plugin learning from actual verified changes, with file/symbol modes; context_files must NOT be a training dependency or automatically mutated. Work only in orbit-graph; no Orbit control-plane crate dependencies or internal database reads. Preserve current graph/CLI behavior. No releases, tags, publication, or agent-review automation. Keep modules readable and cohesive. Run CONTRIBUTING.md checks, strict Clippy/fmt/tests/docs/build and real CLI tests; leave changes for managed delivery.

Stage 3 of 3. Finish the approved product using prior history/recommendation APIs. Implement a proper Orbit external tool plugin with versioned *.orbit-tool.yaml manifests and JSON stdin/stdout contract, discovered from current Orbit crates/orbit-cli/src/command/tool/{manifest,scaffold,add}.rs and crates/orbit-cli/assets/tool_templates/external_tool.py.tmpl. Expose recommendation and index status plus deliberate sync/import maintenance. Provide install/uninstall instructions/scripts and an agent skill explaining query/task-ID, level file|symbol, evidence and freshness. This is an Orbit plugin, not merely a Codex app plugin; do not substitute an unregistered binary for end-to-end proof.

Build authoritative read adapter/export integration for Orbit task metadata and delivered evidence. First discover current exposed task/search/workflow interfaces, explicit workspace selection and command protocol. No direct Orbit SQLite/task-bundle reads, cwd authority guessing, shadow task store or fabricated verified delivery labels. Reuse existing hybrid search where available; support versioned exported data and label lexical/offline fallback honestly. Use task PR references plus verified merged commit/base and Git evidence when no bulk delivery feed is exposed; provenance ties public task records to exact delivery revisions. Cursor/bounded pagination/partial coverage must be explicit so a newest-N list is not represented as full corpus. Support practical incremental synchronization from configured authority, not hand-editing JSON as the only user path. If a truly necessary Orbit-side read seam is missing, document exact schema/capability requirement for an orchestrator successor, do not modify Orbit in this task or silently reduce functionality.

Implement chronological backtest command/harness: training deliveries strictly precede held-out task-time cutoff; pre-execution task text only; no target delivery leakage in co-change, ID resolution or graph snapshot. Compare combined ranking with task-search-only, graph-only, and simple frequency baselines. Report file and symbol recall@K, precision@K, stale-result rate, latency, coverage/exclusions and exact input/revision provenance. Run synthetic adversarial fixtures and a bounded real Orbit repository corpus from authoritative exported task data with verified Git changes. Record measured results without claiming superiority absent evidence. Add reproducible result artifact/docs, installation and end-user examples, CI for new behavioral paths; preserve no-release policy.

Validate actual installed Orbit plugin tool invocation in an isolated test configuration, then production registration is orchestrator-owned. Use current installed orbit binary for integration tests, not the hazardous broad Orbit test suite. Plugin callable by agent via Orbit and realistic query/task-ID both modes must be demonstrated.
acceptance_criteria: Orbit external tool manifests and executable protocol pass actual installed Orbit tool registration/invocation in isolated config; recommendation/status and setup/removal documented.

A runnable authoritative Orbit data adapter supplies task text, verified change associations and optional hybrid hits using explicit workspace/repository routing; sync is bounded/incremental with honest partial coverage and no private-store coupling.

Chronological evaluation reports all four ranking variants and file/symbol recall/precision@K, stale rate, latency, exclusions and source provenance; target/future leakage tests pass; a bounded real corpus evaluation is recorded.
Real plugin/query/task-ID file and symbol workflows, installation docs and CI validated; no required integration gap is called complete or hidden behind synthetic fixtures.
